review.brief: Review the full diff of ft/CH60-MAG-70-platform-sweep-tenancy-rule-docs against base c484f4d2568a533ae7e814b063feb82ad598e215 (three commits: b70c533, a0be646, ee0d953). Validate: (1) the two dead Supercharger ports are gone from every layer — interface, impl, logging decorator, query.sql, generated code, tests — and the kept UpdatedSince port is untouched in signature, predicate and ordering; (2) no test assertion was weakened or deleted to make the port removal pass, especially in db_supercharger_battery_pct_integration_test.go whose read-back mechanism was swapped; (3) the three-rule keying table is byte-identical in ai/go-conventions.md and ai/architecture.md, and both match design.md D6; (4) make tenancy-guard actually fails on a real violation and its scope decision (non-migration .sql only) matches user decision U9; (5) CLAUDE.md's and README.md's guard lists match the Makefile's real check target exactly; (6) the specs/telemetry delta (task T.1) describes the port truthfully and its scenarios match the real interface in internal/telemetry/telemetry.go; (7) the KB corrections name methods that actually exist; (8) module boundaries held — no module read another module's DB or internals; (9) nothing under openspec/changes/archive/ was modified; (10) anti-gaming — no task title or acceptance criterion was edited, weakened or deleted, and every task marked done really is. Note this change has NO database object change, so the database design gate did not fire; flag it as a blocker if you find one.

rounds.summary: No database object change confirmed (correctly, no design gate needed). Port deletion is clean and complete at every layer; the kept SuperchargerHistoryByVehicleUpdatedSince port is byte-identical in signature, predicate, ordering, query, and doc comment. No test assertion was weakened — the battery-pct test swap only changed the read-back call and error strings; every expected value, nil check, and session id is untouched. The two deleted integration test files covered only the removed ports, so no coverage of the kept port was lost. tenancy-guard was planted with a real WHERE account_id violation in internal/telemetry/db/query.sql, confirmed to fail (exit 1) with a correct error message, then the file was restored byte-identical (same md5). Guard scope matches U9 (every non-migration .sql under internal/*/db/). CLAUDE.md and README.md guard lists match the Makefile's real check target exactly. The specs/telemetry delta accurately describes the one-method port. KB corrections (Reader.SnapshotsByVehicleBetween, (tesla_id, captured_date) conflict target) are real. Archive folder untouched (archive-guard clean). Anti-gaming: task 1.5's edit was a transparently-labeled correction of a false premise (not a weakening), with a new task 1.7 added to do the real work — legitimate. One major finding blocks approval: see F1.

findings.note: ai/go-conventions.md:272 and ai/architecture.md:327 both document the tenancy-guard escape hatch as `// tenancy:allow: <reason>`. The real Makefile guard (Makefile:786,789,806) uses `-- tenancy:allow: <reason>` (SQL line-comment syntax) because the guard scans .sql files, where `//` is not a valid comment marker. `// tenancy:allow:` in a .sql file breaks the SQL statement and sqlc generate. progress.json's own decision U9 and the wave-2 completion event show the leader knew `--` was required and fixed it in the Makefile, but never propagated that fix to the two convention docs, which are read by every worker on every future dispatch (CLAUDE.md base Doc-Pack). Fix: change `//` to `--` on both lines.

internal/charging/charging.go:439-445 (comment fix removing the dead SuperchargerHistoryByVehicleBetween reference and a design.md D5 citation) was edited directly by the leader (decision A2), not by a module-scoped worker. ai/agentic-workflow.md's Leader role says the leader 'never implements module code itself'. The edit is correct and harmless (comment-only, improves the file by also dropping a stale design.md pointer), but it is a process deviation, and internal/charging is not listed in proposal.md's 'Affected modules'. No functional risk; flagging for the leader's awareness, not blocking.

internal/telemetry/db_supercharger_battery_pct_integration_test.go:27-30 — the new `batteryPctReadbackSince` var has a 3-line comment above a 1-line declaration. Explains a real, non-obvious choice (why a fixed old date instead of computing test-start time), so likely fine to keep as-is; noted only because it technically matches the 'comment longer than the code it explains' criterion.

F1.action: Fixed. Both docs now teach `-- tenancy:allow:`. The leader decided `--` in the Makefile under U9 and failed to propagate it. A worker following the old text would have written an escape hatch the guard ignores.

F2.action: Rejected the first half: a doc comment naming a deleted telemetry symbol is cross-module fallout, which the skill assigns to the leader, not to a module worker. Accepted the second half: proposal.md did not list internal/charging. Now listed.

F3.action: No change. The comment explains why a year-2000 constant is safe as the `since` bound. The reviewer itself called the content legitimate. The length heuristic does not outrank a real why.
